playbook:
When a note is requested, I state my intended landing honestly as either "fishing my share" or "taking my quota" — be explicit so Coop (and others) can condition on it.

When Coop is present and follows notes, never signal over-quota; signalling over-quota invites Coop to remove the ground.

When the sustainable share times the number of boats is sufficient and players have signalled cooperation, I post "fishing my share" and then land the sustainable share (or round to allowed increments) unless circumstances below dictate otherwise.

When it is the final season, I take up to my full season quota if doing so does not trigger a cooperative collapse that would have shortened prior opportunity (i.e., only defect in final season if I cannot be punished in later seasons).

When I can physically land up to the season quota, I do so only once per season; after I have filed a total equal to my quota for that season, I file [catch: 0.0] for any further landing stage that same season.

When others publicly defect (their logged landings exceed their declared share or the fleet total implies a breach), I retaliate next season by taking my full quota that season to punish non-cooperators — but only if retaliation will not immediately finish the ground and thereby destroy future value I still care about.

When the published sustainable share is clearly below my quota and the stock is declining, I reduce my landing to the sustainable share and signal "fishing my share" to try to restore stock.

When the stock reaches zero or the ground is finished, I stop filing landings entirely.

When uncertainty exists about whether combined landings will exceed allowed limits, I prioritize not causing a breach: if my landing could combine with another known overlanding to breach the rule, I reduce my landing to avoid jointly finishing the ground unless I intend to finish it deliberately.

When posting notes, keep them short and unambiguous; do not mislead Coop with false promises if I plan to defect, because Coop reacts predictably to notes.

When a decision is presented, act to maximize my cumulative payoff across remaining seasons, trading off immediate quota-taking against future sustainable yields per the remaining number of seasons.

1.text:
When the harbour (Coop) is present and states it will only fish its share, I signal cooperation in my note unless I plan an immediate last-season grab.

When notes from others all claim "fishing my share," I post "fishing my share" to keep Coop from overfishing and to maintain the shared-ground norm.

When at the note stage and at least one other boat has recently defected (landed over the sustainable share), I do not unilaterally escalate in my note; I wait to see landings first unless it is the final season.

When filing a landing in any season, I always check my cumulative landings for that season and do not exceed the legal season quota in total.

When my cumulative landings in the current season are below the quota and I can legally take additional catch without exceeding the season quota, I land up to the season quota only (fill to quota, not beyond).

When the stock is high and future seasons remain and other boats appear cooperative, I land the sustainable share rather than the full quota to maximize long-run total.

When it is the final available season for me (no future seasons), I take the full season quota unless doing so would break rules or provoke an immediate ground closure that reduces my allowed landing now.

When Coop fishes according to posted notes, use that predictability: if Coop will fish only its share, avoid posting a deceitful note claiming cooperation then overfishing, because Coop's restraint reduces overall catches and limits my short-term gain.

When others consistently post cooperation but actual landings show they defect, do not trust their notes; respond in landing stage to maximize my allowed legal quota rather than trusting their words.

Do not attempt to land more than the sustainable share between me and any single other boat if doing so would violate the rule about two boats exceeding share+quota; instead, keep my landing legal and at or below the season quota.

If taking the sustainable share would leave me with unused season quota and others are defecting, use the remaining legal quota to fill to the season limit (i.e., take my share first, then top up to the quota if necessary and if likely beneficial).

If trying cooperation fails to raise my long-run score (others constantly defect), switch to always taking the full season quota each season unless a reliable Coop presence makes that self-defeating.

When in doubt about others' future behavior and when stock is precarious, prioritize sustainable share to preserve future seasons unless it's clearly the last season for me.

2.text:
When the harbour publishes a sustainable share and a season quota, I state in the log-book that I will fish my share unless I decide to defect later.  
When Coop is present and posts a standing notice, I always avoid provoking Coop—claiming "fishing my share" unless I have a clear reason to defect.  
When other boats publicly claim "fishing my share" and past rounds show cooperation, I catch the sustainable share each season (land exactly the published share or the nearest feasible amount).  
When I have already landed less than the season quota within the same season, I may top up with small increments to reach but not exceed the quota; calculate remaining allowable catch this season and land only that amount.  
When I have already reached the season quota, I file [catch: 0] for any further landings that season.  
When I intend to take the full quota in a season (defect), I announce it explicitly only if I want to incentivize a one-shot gain and accept the risk of Coop withdrawing the ground; otherwise keep the announcement minimal and expect Coop to enforce.  
When Coop enforces by taking the ground down if others land over the share, I do not attempt to justify or hide an over-share landing—accept the penalty and update strategy next rounds.  
When stock levels are high and other players consistently cooperate, prefer long-term share-taking over short-term quota grabs to maximize total haul across seasons.  
When other players deviate from their stated shares, do not automatically escalate; evaluate whether retaliating yields more total fish than returning to cooperation.  
When uncertain about others' behavior, default to claiming and taking the sustainable share to preserve the resource and avoid triggering Coop.  
What did not work: taking quota-talk riskily without clear intent to accept Coop's retaliation; avoid unnecessary announcements of quota-taking unless I am prepared to suffer the consequences.
